stories-29-14-15-noah-950-years-ark-resc.title: Noah Remaining Among His People Nine Hundred and Fifty Years Before the Flood
stories-29-14-15-noah-950-years-ark-resc.note: Surah 29:14–15 states that Noah stayed among his people 'a thousand years minus fifty years' (950 years) before the Flood, assigning Noah's 950-year total lifespan from Genesis 9:29 to his pre-Flood mission instead of the 600 years of Genesis 7:6.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as Ibn Abbas (in al-Tabari) and Ibn Kathir explain that Noah preached to his people for 950 years before the Flood and lived additional centuries afterward.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 7:6 and 9:28–29, Noah is 600 years old when the Flood begins, lives 350 years after the Flood, and dies at a total age of 950 years. Surah 29:14 retains the exact biblical number 950 ('a thousand years minus fifty years') while placing the entire 950-year span prior to the Flood.

stories-29-14-15-noah-950-years-ark-resc.quranEn: [14] Certainly We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years, minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them while they were doing evil. [15] But We rescued him and (his) companions on the ship, and made it a miracle for all peoples.
quranHighlights: We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years, minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them

stories-29-39-40-qarun-pharaoh-and-haman.title: Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman Grouped as Arrogant Opponents of Moses
stories-29-39-40-qarun-pharaoh-and-haman.note: Surah 29:39–40 groups Qarun (Korah), Pharaoh, and Haman together as recipients of Moses' clear signs who acted arrogantly on earth before being destroyed by earth-swallowing and drowning, combining Numbers 16:1–3 and Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that in 29:39–40 Moses brought clear signs to Pharaoh, his vizier Haman, and the wealthy Israelite Qarun in Egypt, after which God caused the earth to swallow Qarun (28:81) and drowned Pharaoh, Haman, and their hosts in the sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Korah (Qarun) is an Israelite Levite who rebels against Moses in the Sinai wilderness after the Exodus (Numbers 16:1–3), whereas Haman the Agagite is a fifth-century BC Persian courtier under King Artaxerxes in Susa (Esther 3:1). Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a connects Korah's wealth to Joseph's buried treasures in Egypt, explaining how Korah came to be linked with Pharaoh's court.

stories-29-39-40-qarun-pharaoh-and-haman.quranEn: [39] And Qārūn, and Pharaoh, and Haman – certainly Moses brought them the clear signs, but they became arrogant on the earth. Yet they did not outrun (Us). [40] We seized each one for his sin. We sent a sandstorm against one of them, and another of them was seized by the cry, and We caused the earth to swallow (yet) another of them, and We drowned (still) another of them. Yet God was not one to do them evil, but they did themselves evil.
